_comment: Stable GAME-STATE -> art-FOLDER mapping for the two heroes. The game (games2/scripts/build-manifest.mjs) reads THIS file instead of hardcoding PixelLab folder names, so when an animation is renamed on PixelLab the game keeps working and ONLY this file changes. Maintained by the characters2 agent and validated on every sync by characters2/pipeline/verify_sync.py (which fails if any mapped folder is missing). Keys under `states` are the game's logical animation names; values are the folder under humans/<hero>/animations/. `overrides.<hero>` wins where that hero's folder name differs from the default.
_maintenance: After a sync, run: python characters2/pipeline/verify_sync.py  (it checks every hero x state resolves to a real folder). If PixelLab renames a move, update the value here — nothing in games2 needs to change.
_changelog: 2026-07-29: full animation overhaul — idle/walk/run replaced by custom cycles (Calm idle / Full walk / Full run); ONE jump only (maintainer): the old `jump` (high-jump, deleted on PixelLab) and `runjump` states are consolidated into a single `jump` state mapped to the steeplechase run-jump.

npcs._comment: GAME STATE -> animation folder for NPCs (npcs/<folder>/animations/<slug>). PixelLab animation names are GENERATION PROMPTS — the maintainer rewords them freely to coax the right motion out of the model, so they vary and contain typos (152 NPCs say 'still', 40 say 'stilI' with a capital i). The game must NEVER depend on that text. sync.py resolves each state here and PUBLISHES the result as `states` on npcs/<folder>/character.json and in npcs/index.json; consumers read states.idle and never guess. verify_sync.py fails if a required state does not resolve for every NPC.
npcs._maintenance: A state matches an animation when its slug contains ANY keyword (lowercased). If several match, the richest wins (most frames, then most directions, then slug order) — deterministic. Pin an exact folder with overrides.<npc folder>.<state> when keywords can't decide. Adding a state (walk, talk, work...) is one entry here — no code change.
